This application under Section 430 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 has been filed seeking suspension of sentence of the applicants/accused nos.1 and 2 (A1 and A2) in S.C.No.215/2021 on the file of the Court of Session, Thalassery.

They have been found guilty of the offences punishable under Sections 376D and 376(2)(1) IPC and Sections 3(a) read with Section 4;
Section 5(g) and Section 5(k) read with Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

sentences.text: They have been sentenced to varying terms of imprisonment for the aforesaid offences.
The sentences have been directed to run concurrently.
The maximum period of imprisonment they will in have to undergo is 20 years.

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicants/A1 and A2 that though the incident is alleged to have taken place on 23/12/2017 at 02:00 p.m., the FIS was given after an inordinate delay of nearly four years, that is, on 04/01/2021.
The applicants/A1 and A2 are none other than the neighbours of PW4 the victim.
On 25/02/2018 PW4, the victim went missing.
Thereafter she was traced by the police on 01/03/2018, on which day she was found to be hiding in the attic of her maternal grandmother's home.
Thereafter, she was sent to the shelter home.

After PW4 was traced out, five crimes were registered by the Alakode police, that is, crime nos.161/2018, 162/2018,
163/2018, 164/2018 and 165/2018, at which time the names of the accused persons were never disclosed.
The medical evidence also does not in any way support the prosecution case of sexual intercourse by several persons.

The learned counsel also points out to the in testimony of PW5, the father who has a case that though his daughter had stated to the police that the accused persons had also raped her, it was much thereafter he realised that no crimes had been registered.
The learned counsel draws my attention to the testimony of PW16 the investigating officer, who deposed that no such statement had been given either by PW4 or PW5 her father.
Hence, he submits that a lenient view may be taken and the sentence may be suspended.
3. The application is opposed by the learned Public Prosecutor, who submits that the background from which PW4 comes must also be taken into account by the court when her testimony is appreciated.

It was also pointed out that the argument that there is no medical evidence to support the prosecution case is incorrect because PW9 in her re-examination clarified that the possibility of sexual intercourse by multiple persons cannot be ruled out.
My attention was also drawn to paragraph no.27 of the in impugned judgment, where the trial court discusses the testimony of PW11, the counsellor.

In such circumstances, it is submitted that evidence of PW4 has to be appreciated in the said background and merely because there is delay in the crime being reported, is no ground to disbelieve the testimony of PW4 or take a lenient view in granting an order of suspension.
4. Heard both sides.
5. I was taken through the testimony of PW4, the victim as well as PW9, the doctor.
The medical evidence on record does raise doubts regarding the multiple rape to which PW4 is alleged to have been subjected to.
As rightly pointed out by the learned Public Prosecutor, mere delay is no reason to disbelieve the prosecution case.
However, it needs to be noted that in the year 2018, 5 crimes were registered at which time also the names of the accused persons are not seen revealed.
The stand of PW4 and PW5 that they had in fact stated to the police that the in applicants/A1 and A2 herein had also raped the victim is not supported by PW16 the investigating officer.

There is an allegation that it was only in 2021 when PW4 came home and her father informed that no crime had been registered against the applicants/A1 and A2 that she realized that no action had been taken by the police against the said persons.
The relevant portion of the testimony of PW4 was also brought to my notice which shows that she did come home several times after 2018.
Evidence has also come on record that she had undergone counselling on many days during her stay in the shelter home also.
In the facts and circumstances of the case and taking into account the fact that the appeal is of the year 2024 there is no possibility of the appeal being taken up for hearing in the near future
